summary: Ukrainian peasant anarchist Nestor Makhno, jailed as a teenage militant under the Tsar, led a guerrilla army that held a self-governing free territory in eastern Ukraine, fighting Whites, occupiers and Bolsheviks from 1917 to 1921.

evidence.note: framed as the annual Christmas hero episode after Wallenberg and John Brown
long background on Ukraine as a colonized land and Catherine II's land grants
1906-07 armed expropriations of local businessmen and shootout with police
death sentence commuted; years of hard labor in Tsarist prison, reads Kropotkin
released in 1917, returns home and organizes peasant unions and land seizures
Mennonite self-defense militia sides with Austro-German occupiers in 1918 reprisals
flees to Moscow and meets Lenin before slipping back into Ukraine
extended account of White Army pogroms and atrocities under Denikin
September 1919 counterattack at Peregonovka routs Denikin's forces
final war with the Red Army to August 1921, then exile via Poland to Paris
dies sick and isolated in Paris; death year garbled in transcript, 1934 from knowledge

notes: Hero episode, so the lifetime rule applies (1888-1934); main_span 1917-1921 per the encyclopedia test, though the 1906-1908 militant youth also gets long airtime. Birth and death years garbled in the transcript, filled from knowledge. Primary civil-war over protest-revolution per its exclude_when. Ukraine colonial background is pre-story context, kept as a theme only. UA-23 is Zaporizhzhia Oblast (Huliaipole).
